ModelCharacter: The defining C-Dory pocket cruiser: an exceptionally light, shallow-draft, trailerable pilothouse boat with a nearly flat aft planing surface, single outboard and simple four-person cabin. It trades deep-V ride comfort for low-speed planing, fuel efficiency, easy towing and beachable go-anywhere utility.
DesignLineage: C-Dory states that the 22 Cruiser was introduced in January 1987 and remains its most successful model.
The 22 Angler uses the same basic hull but shifts cabin length aft-to-forward tradeoff toward a much larger cockpit.
The hull is nearly flat at the stern with increasing V toward the bow and deep reverse chines; it is not a displacement trawler despite its salty appearance.
Continuous production has brought material and interior refinements without breaking the core 22 Cruiser lineage.
OwnershipCharacter: One of the simplest cruising boats in B-Atlas: one outboard, minimal plumbing, shallow draft and easy trailering. The key survey issue on older examples is moisture intrusion into cored structures, especially around cockpit/fuel-tank fasteners and owner-added hardware.

ModelCharacter: The best-known Cape Dory powerboat: a compact New England flybridge cruiser with a lobster-boat-derived semi-displacement hull, full protective keel, single inboard and unusually yacht-like teak interior for 28 feet.
DesignLineage: The Cape Dory 28 power family was introduced in the mid-1980s as the company's first major pleasure-power line.
Factory literature identifies four related configurations on the same hull: Flybridge Cruiser, Power Cruiser, Open Fisherman and 280 Sport.
The Flybridge Cruiser adds an upper helm to the enclosed Power Cruiser arrangement and became the best-known version.
More than 220 Cape Dory 28 powerboats were built across the family, representing roughly three-quarters of Cape Dory's pleasure-power production.
OwnershipCharacter: A mechanically simple classic cruiser with protected single-shaft propulsion and good deck access. Core moisture, windows, aging tanks, old Volvo/Chrysler installations and flybridge structure are more important ownership variables than system complexity.

You need multiple private staterooms

ModelCharacter: The enclosed two-cabin sister to Fjord's modern open-deck performance boats: a Patrick Banfield/Jim Wilshire design created as a smaller companion to the 40 Cruiser, combining minimalist Scandinavian styling, twin diesel performance and a weather-protected main-deck living space.
DesignLineage: The Fjord 36 Cruiser was announced in 2007 for launch in the 2008 season as the smaller sister to the Fjord 40 Cruiser.
It was designed by Patrick Banfield and Jim Wilshire/Allseas Design, with interior work by Mark Tucker.
The 36 Cruiser shares the modern Fjord design language with the 36 Open but is a distinct enclosed-cruising layout rather than merely an Open with a hardtop.
Published owner-club records give a broader 2005–2012 production window, but contemporary launch reporting supports 2008 as the reliable introduction point; B-Atlas therefore uses 2008–2012.
OwnershipCharacter: Twin diesels and enclosed accommodation make it a much more substantial cruising proposition than the Open. It remains performance-oriented, so sterndrive/drive-train service, glazing, ventilation and tightly packaged machinery matter more than slow-speed economy.
